videos.caption: I take women’s rights seriously, so this is one of the first things I asked about while visiting Ghardaïa, Algeria  Now this is not necessarily for any reason. It has nothing to do with religion or location. The only thing it has to do with is that many communities that are small and follow old traditions typically give less rights and protections to women. However, I was pleasantly surprised that this is not the case in Ghardaia.   I really appreciate what I learned about  Mozabite communities, giving women in their own committees and ability to make decisions for themselves. When it comes to dress, extra protections, to feel safe and comfortable in their marriages, and the community standing in solidarity with its women. Everything is closed… and I mean everything 😳🇩🇿 Walking through the city center on a Friday in Algeria felt like a ghost town. Shops were shuttered, businesses were closed, and the streets were much quieter than expected. As a traveler, it was a huge culture shock—but it’s all part of the country’s Friday traditions. Would this surprise you too? Watch until the end to see what Algeria looks like on a Friday. #Algeria #AlgeriaTravel #TravelAlgeria #FridayInAlgeria #cultureshock
